questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 240 respectively. If one of the number is 24, what is the another number
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

H.C.F and L.C.M = 12 and 240 and one number = 24

**FORMULA USED:**

H.C.F × L.C.M = Product of one number and another number

**CALCULATION:**

H.C.F and L.C.M = 12 and 240 and one number = 24

H.C.F × L.C.M = Product of one number and another number

⇒ 12 × 240 = 24 × another number

⇒ another number = 120

**∴ the another number = 120**

questions.question: Rama and Hari can together finish a piece of work in 15 day. Rama works twice as fast as Hari, then Hari alone can finish work in :
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Rama and Hari together can finish a piece of work in 15 days

Rama works twice as fast as Hari

**FORMULA USED:**

 Work = Efficiency × No. of days

**CALCULATION:**

Rama works twice as fast as Hari

⇒ The efficiency of Rama: Hari = 2:1

⇒ Total Work = Efficiency of (Rama + Hari) × Total number of days to finish the work

⇒ 3 × 15 = 45

⇒ No. of days required to finish whole work by Hari alone = Total work/Efficiency

⇒ 45/1 = 45

**∴ Hari can finish the whole work alone in 45 Days**

questions.question: A trader allows two successive discounts of 5% each on the marked price of a sofa set for ₹24,500. The selling price of sofa set is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two successive discounts are 5%

The marked Price is Rs24,500

**Formula Used:**

Net Discount % = (– X – Y + XY/100),

Where X and Y are two successive discounts.

S.P = M.P × (100 – D%)/100

Where,

SP is Selling price,

MP is Marked price,

D is Discount

**Calculation:**

Using the formula, Net Discount,

⇒ – 5 – 5 + 25/100

⇒ – 10 + .25

⇒ – 9.75%

S.P = M.P × (100 - D%)/100

⇒ S.P = 24,500 × (100 - 9.75)/100

⇒ S.P = 24,500 × 90.25/100

⇒ S.P = 22,111.25

**∴ Selling Price (S.P) of Sofa is Rs 22,111.25**

questions.question: Shopkeeper selling on article for ₹46 loses 8%. In order to gain of 6%, what should be the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Shopkeeper selling on article for ₹46 loses 8%

**Concept Used:**

Selling price = Cost price – Loss

Selling price = Cost price + profit

**Calculation:**

Let cost price of the article is 100%

Loss is 8%

Selling price (100 – 8) = 92%

Accordingly,

92% = 46

⇒ 100% = (46/92) × 100

⇒ 100% = 50

Cost price of the article is Rs. 50

He has to gain 6%

Selling price should be (100 + 6) = 106%

100% = 50

⇒ 106% = (50/100) × 106

⇒ 106% = 53

**∴**** In order to gain of 6%, the selling price of the article should be Rs. 53**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

Let the CP be Rs. 100

Now he sold for 8% loss,

⇒ SP = (100 – 8)/100 × 100

⇒ SP = 92

According to the question,

⇒ 92 = 46

⇒ 1 = 46/92 = 1/2 ----(I)

Now he sold at 6% profit,

New SP = (100 + 6)/100 × 100

⇒ New SP = 106

Using result (I), we get

New SP = 106 × 1/2 = 53

∴ In order to gain of 6%, the selling price of the article should be Rs. 53

questions.question: The areas of two squares are 16 : 9. The ratio of their perimeter is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of areas of two squares is 16 : 9

**Concept Used:**

Area of square = side × side

The perimeter of square = 4 × side

**Calculation:**

Area of 1st square/Area of 2ⁿd square = 16/9

⇒ (side × side) of 1st square/(side × side) of 2ⁿd square = 16/9

⇒ side of 1st square/side of 2ⁿd square = √(16/9)

⇒ side of 1st square/side of 2ⁿd square = 4/3

Side of 1st square is 4k [Where ‘k’ is a constant]

Side of 2ⁿd square is 3k [Where ‘k’ is a constant]

The perimeter of 1st square is 4 × 4k = 16k

The perimeter of 2ⁿd square is 4 × 3k = 12k

The ratio of the perimeter of two square is 16k : 12K

⇒ 16 : 12

**∴**** The ratio of their perimeter is 16 : 12**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** Area of square = a²

perimeter of square = 4a

⇒ 16 : 9

⇒ (4)² : (3)²

Perimeter = 4 × 4 : 4 × 3

⇒ 16 : 12

∴ The ratio of their perimeter is 16 : 12

questions.question: In a class, the average age of 40 students is 12 years when teacher’s age is included to it, the average increases by 1. The age of teacher is :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average age of 40 students is 12 years

When the teacher’s age is included to it, the average increases by 1

**Concept Used:**

Sum of all quantity = Average × Number of quantities

**Calculation:**

The average age of 40 students is 12 years

Sum of the age of 40 students is 40 × 12 = 480 years

When the teacher’s age is included to it, the average increases by 1

Then average age (12 + 1) = 13 years and total number of man is (40 + 1) = 41

Then total age = (41 × 13) years

⇒ 533 years

Age of the teacher is (533 – 480) = 53 years

 

 

__**Alternative Method:**__

Average age increased by 1 years

Total age increase of 40 students is 40 years

New average age = (12 + 1) = 13 year

∴ age of the teacher = (40 + 13) = 53 years

questions.question: The compound interest on an amount for 2 years at 5% per annum compounded annually is ₹205. The simple interest is:
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Time(n) = 2 years, Rate(R) = 5% per annum and Interest(I) = Rs205

**FORMULA USED:**

A = P (1 + R/100)ⁿ 

Where A → Amounts → (Principal + Interest),

P → Principal

R → Rate per annum

n → Number of years

Simple Interest (S.I) = P × R × T/100

**CALCULATION:**

A = P (1 + R/100)n

⇒ (P + 205) = P (1 + 5/100)²

⇒ (P + 205) = P (1 + 1/20)²

⇒ (P + 205) = P × 21/20 × 21/20

⇒ P + 205 = 441P/400

⇒ 205 = - P + 441P/400

⇒ 205 = 41P/400

⇒ P = Rs 2000 

Simple Interest (S.I) = P × R × T/100

⇒ S.I = 2000 × 5 × 2/100

**∴ Simple Interest is Rs200.**

questions.question: In how many years, a sum will be thrice of it at the rate of interest 5% per annum?
questions.solution:

The sum will be thrice of it. Rate of interest is 5%

**Concept Used:**

The simple interest of a principal p at the rate of interest r% in t years is (prt/100)

**Calculation:**

The sum will be thrice of the principal, that means interest will be double of the principal

Let, principal, is p and time is t years

Rate of interest is 5%

(p × t × 5)/100 = 2p

⇒ Pt/20 = 2p

⇒ t = 2 × 20

⇒ t = 40

**∴**** In 40 year the sum will be thrice of it at the rate of interest 5% per annum.**

questions.question: ‘A’ pipe can empty a tank in 20 minutes. The second pipe ‘B’ has a diameter twice as that of ‘A’. If both A & B pipe are attached to the tank how much time will be required to empty the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can empty the tank in 20 minutes and

Pipe B has a diameter twice as that of A

i.e Pipe B has twice the efficiency of Pipe A

**Formula Used:**

Total Capacity = Efficiency × Time

**Concept used:**

The efficiency of a pipe is directly proportional to,

The square of the radius of the pipe

**Calculation:**

The ratio of the diameter of A and B = 1 ∶ 2

The ratio of the radius of pipe A and B = 1/2 ∶ 2/2 

The ratio of the radius of pipe A and B = 1 ∶ 2

Now by using the concept,

The ratio of efficiency of A and B = 1² ∶ 2² 

The ratio of efficiency of A and B = 1 : 4

Time is taken by pipe A to empty the tank = 20 minutes

Total Capacity = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = 20 × 1 = 20 litre

When both Pipe A & B start together,

Then they can empty the whole tank in,

⇒ Total Capacity/Efficiency of both pipe

⇒ 20/(4 + 1)

⇒ 20/5

⇒ 4

**∴ Time Required to empty the tank is 4 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Pipe A circle area = (π D/2)²

Pipe B circle area = (π 2D/2)²

The efficiency of pipes A and B

⇒ (π D/2)² = (π 2D/2)2

⇒ 1 : 4

Total capacity of tank = 20 × 1 = 20 litres 

When both Pipe A & B start together,

Then they can empty the whole tank in,

⇒ Total Capacity/Efficiency of both pipe

⇒ 20/(4 + 1)

⇒ 20/5

⇒ 4

∴ The time required to empty the tank is 4 min.
